tagline: Up the Payette from the Snake, through the Gem of Plenty.
intro: Idaho 52 starts near the mouth of the Payette, where native tribes gathered their winter food, and follows the river east through Payette and Emmett, then up Black Canyon past the diversion dam of the early 1920s to Horseshoe Bend. Ruts of the Goodale Trail can still be seen along the way.
Settlers bound west for land came this way, passing others headed east for the gold and silver fields. The Falk store site marks what was the only stage stop between Boise and Umatilla, Oregon.

moments.title: Payette
moments.text: Payette began as Boomerang, a railroad camp where logs floated down the river to be sawn into ties, and took the name of a fur trader remembered as a large, merry man.

moments.title: Emmett
moments.text: Emmett grew up around a ferry crossing on the Payette, and in the early 1900s its fruit packers labeled the valley the Gem of Plenty.

moments.title: Horseshoe Bend
moments.text: The town sits on a horseshoe turn of the Payette and began as a camp where prospectors waited for the snow to melt off the Boise Basin gold country.
